{{short description|Japanese-American mathematician}}
{{Lead too short|date=October 2021}}
'''Kiyoshi Igusa''' (born November 28, 1949) is a Japanese-American mathematician and a professor at [[Brandeis University]]. He works in [[representation theory]] and [[topology]].

== Education and career ==
He studied at the [[University of Chicago]] and [[Princeton University]], where he obtained his [[Ph.D.]] in 1979, under the direction of [[Allen Hatcher]] and [[Wu-Chung Hsiang]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.brandeis.edu/~igusa/myCV2019.pdf|title=CV at Brandeis University}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy| id=23349}}</ref>

From 1981 to 1983, he was a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Fellow]], and since 2012 he is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list#i|title=List of AMS fellows}}</ref>

In 1990, he gave an invited lecture at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Kyoto (Topology Section).<ref name=":ICM">[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Kiyoshi ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers]</ref>

== Personal life==
Igusa's father, [[Jun-Ichi Igusa]], was also a mathematician. Igusa is married to [[Gordana Todorov]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/baltimoresun/obituary.aspx?n=yoshie-igusa&pid=192987402&fhid=20867|title=Yoshie Igusa, 1927 – 2019|newspaper=Baltimore Sun|date=May 26, 2019|via=Legacy.com}}</ref> with whom he is a frequent collaborator.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://homepage.divms.uiowa.edu/~shijzhu/IowaGT70-E.pdf|title=40 years of collaboration with Gordana|first=Kiyoshi|last=Igusa|author-link=Kiyoshi Igusa|date=August 2019}}{{Dead link|date=June 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
